surface_mechanism_description: The growth of wurtzite GaN on (0 0 1) GaAs substrates by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) involves the use of trimethylgallium (TMG) and ammonia (NH3) as Ga and N sources. The GaN films are grown at temperatures between 500 and 650 °C, with a nitridation step prior to growth. The growth process is limited by the dose to one monolayer per cycle, and the bond energy of Ga-N is higher than Ga-Ga, leading to the decomposition of Ga dimers and bonding to nitrogen atoms on the surface to form GaN molecules during the growth process.
evidence: The bond energy of Ga±N is higher than Ga±Ga, Ga dimers decompose and bond to nitrogen atoms on the surface to form GaN molecules during the growth process.
